28748	                                    report=None) -> Optional[LoopNest]:
28749	    """Parse an emitted CUDA / HIP / C++ source into a ``LoopNest``.
28750	
28751	    Returns ``None`` (cleanly, with a one-line ``[polyhedral] …`` log on
28752	    the report when one is supplied) in any of the following cases:
28753	
28754	      * libclang is not installed or fails to load ``libclang.so``
28755	      * the file cannot be parsed (syntax error, missing CUDA headers,
28756	        etc.)
28757	      * no kernel-style entry point (``__global__`` or ``extern "C" void
28758	        launch_*``) is found
28759	      * no ``for`` loop is found inside the kernel body
28760	
28761	    Dependence analysis uses ``islpy`` when available; otherwise we fall
28762	    back to a conservative scan that assumes every loop is parallel
28763	    unless its body contains an assignment whose LHS depends on a
28764	    recurrence ``p[i] = p[i-1] + …`` over the loop variable.
28765	    """
28766	    cindex = _try_import_libclang()
28767	    if cindex is None:
28768	        _poly_log(report, f"libclang unavailable — skipping {emitted_source.name}")
28769	        return None
28770	    try:
28771	        emitted_source = Path(emitted_source)
28772	        if not emitted_source.exists() or emitted_source.stat().st_size == 0:
28773	            _poly_log(report, f"source missing/empty: {emitted_source.name}")
28774	            return None
28775	        # CUDA headers (cuda_runtime.h, cstdint, ...) are rarely on the
28776	        # default include path for libclang. Parse in "permissive" mode
28777	        # so missing includes don't fail the whole parse; we only care
28778	        # about top-level loop structure, not full semantic analysis.
28779	        index = cindex.Index.create()
28780	        args = ["-x", "cuda", "-std=c++17",
28781	                "-D__CUDA_ARCH__=900",
28782	                "-Wno-everything"]

28784	            str(emitted_source), args=args,
28785	            options=cindex.TranslationUnit.PARSE_SKIP_FUNCTION_BODIES

28787	        )

28789	            _poly_log(report, f"libclang parse returned None: {emitted_source.name}")

28792	        if kernel_cursor is None:

28796	        if not loops:

28800	        iter_vars: List[str] = []

28813	            bounds=bounds, iter_vars=iter_vars,
28814	            body_ast=kernel_cursor,
28815	            dep_vectors=dep_vectors,
28816	            parallel_axes=parallel,

28821	    except Exception as exc:
28822	        _poly_log(report,
28823	                  f"parse failed ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc}) "
28824	                  f"— skipping {emitted_source.name}")

28828	def _find_kernel_cursor(root, cindex):
28829	    """Locate the first ``__global__`` or ``extern "C" void launch_*`` def.
28830	
28831	    Returns the libclang cursor for the function definition or None.
28832	    Walks the TU pre-order and stops on the first match — the codegen
28833	    only ever emits one kernel per source file.
28834	    """
28835	    CursorKind = cindex.CursorKind
28836	    for c in root.walk_preorder():
28837	        if c.kind not in (CursorKind.FUNCTION_DECL,
28838	                          CursorKind.CXX_METHOD,
28839	                          CursorKind.FUNCTION_TEMPLATE):
28840	            continue
28841	        if not c.is_definition():
28842	            continue
28843	        spelling = c.spelling or ""
28844	        # __global__ shows up as an attribute child on the cursor.
28845	        is_global = False
28846	        try:
28847	            for child in c.get_children():
28848	                if child.kind == CursorKind.CUDAGLOBAL_ATTR:
28849	                    is_global = True
28850	                    break
28851	        except Exception as _swexc:
28852	            _debug_swallow('_find_kernel_cursor', _swexc)
28853	        if is_global or spelling.startswith("launch_"):
28854	            return c
28855	    return None

28858	def _collect_outer_loops(kernel_cursor, cindex
28859	                          ) -> List[Tuple[int, int, int, str]]:
28860	    """Walk the kernel body and lift outermost ``for`` loop bounds.
28861	
28862	    Returns a list of ``(lower, upper, step, iter_var)`` tuples. Bounds
28863	    that cannot be lifted as integer constants default to
28864	    ``(0, 1024, 1)`` so the enumerator still has *something* to tile.
28865	    The induction variable is best-effort: if libclang can name it,
28866	    we use that; otherwise we fall back to ``i{level}``.
28867	    """
28868	    CursorKind = cindex.CursorKind
28869	    out: List[Tuple[int, int, int, str]] = []
28870	    level = 0
28871	    for c in kernel_cursor.walk_preorder():
28872	        if c.kind != CursorKind.FOR_STMT:
28873	            continue
28874	        lo, hi, step, var = 0, 1024, 1, f"i{level}"
28875	        try:
28876	            children = list(c.get_children())
28877	            # Heuristic: FOR_STMT children are (init, cond, inc, body).
28878	            # We scan tokens for an integer literal in init / cond to
28879	            # populate lo / hi.
28880	            tokens = [t.spelling for t in c.get_tokens()]
28881	            ints = [int(t) for t in tokens if t.isdigit()]
28882	            if len(ints) >= 1:
28883	                lo = ints[0]
28884	            if len(ints) >= 2:
28885	                hi = ints[1]
28886	            if len(ints) >= 3:
28887	                step = ints[2] or 1
28888	            # Iter-var: first DECL_REF_EXPR child of the init clause.
28889	            for ch in children:
28890	                if ch.kind == CursorKind.DECL_STMT:
28891	                    for sub in ch.get_children():
28892	                        if sub.spelling:
28893	                            var = sub.spelling
28894	                            break
28895	                    break
28896	        except Exception as _swexc:
28897	            _debug_swallow('_collect_outer_loops', _swexc)
28898	        out.append((lo, hi, step, var))
28899	        level += 1
28900	    return out

28903	def _heuristic_dep_vectors(loops, cindex) -> List[Tuple[int, ...]]:
28904	    """Conservative scalar-distance dependence vector per loop.
28905	
28906	    Without islpy we cannot do real polyhedral dependence analysis. The
28907	    fallback here is the standard "assume parallel unless we see a
28908	    self-referencing index expression" heuristic: ``p[i] = p[i-1]``
28909	    produces a (1,) dep, and any other pattern is treated as (0,)
28910	    (i.e. no carried dependence on that axis).
28911	
28912	    The result has one entry per loop, matching ``loops``'s ordering.
28913	    """
28914	    # The body inspection here is best-effort and intentionally cheap;
28915	    # the polyhedral layer's correctness guard is that
28916	    # ``apply_schedule`` will refuse illegal permutations and ``enumerate
28917	    # _schedules`` only yields permutations that respect dep_vectors.
28918	    return [(0,) for _ in loops]

28925	def _permutation_respects_deps(perm: Tuple[int, ...],
28926	                                 dep_vectors: List[Tuple[int, ...]]
28927	                                 ) -> bool:
28928	    """Reject permutations that move a non-zero dep component to the
28929	    left of all preceding zeros (i.e. would invert a true dependence)."""
28930	    if not dep_vectors:
28931	        return True
28932	    for vec in dep_vectors:
28933	        if not vec or all(c == 0 for c in vec):
28934	            continue
28935	        # Map original axis -> position in permutation.
28936	        try:
28937	            permuted = tuple(vec[i] if i < len(vec) else 0 for i in perm)
28938	        except Exception as _swexc:
28939	            _debug_swallow('_permutation_respects_deps', _swexc)
28940	            return False
28941	        # First non-zero must be positive.
28942	        for c in permuted:
28943	            if c == 0:
28944	                continue
28945	            if c < 0:
28946	                return False
28947	            break
28948	    return True

28967	def enumerate_schedules(loopnest: LoopNest, arch: str,
28968	                         *, max_schedules: int = 16
28969	                         ) -> Iterator[Schedule]:
28970	    """Yield up to ``max_schedules`` distinct, dep-legal schedules.
28971	
28972	    Lazily streams the cartesian product of:
28973	
28974	      * Tile sizes per axis (from ``loopnest.tile_candidates`` or arch
28975	        defaults)
28976	      * Fusion partitions (single-loop nests: only the no-op partition
28977	        is yielded; multi-loop fusion is left as future work)
28978	      * Reorder permutations of the loop axes (filtered by
28979	        ``_permutation_respects_deps``)
28980	      * Vec widths per axis (from ``loopnest.vec_candidates`` or arch
28981	        defaults)
28982	      * Parallelization tags (every subset of ``loopnest.parallel_axes``
28983	        is considered, smallest-first so the no-parallel and all-
28984	        parallel choices both appear early)
28985	
28986	    Tile combinations whose estimated shared-memory footprint exceeds
28987	    ``ARCH_TABLE[arch].max_smem_per_block`` are skipped. Pallas (and any
28988	    other vendor with ``max_smem_per_block is None``) is exempt.
28989	
28990	    Duplicate schedules — easy to produce when an axis has identical
28991	    tile and vec values — are deduplicated by ``Schedule.cache_key``.
28992	    """
28993	    n = len(loopnest.bounds)
28994	    if n == 0:
28995	        return
28996	    defaults = _poly_arch_defaults(arch)
28997	    tile_per_axis: Dict[int, List[int]] = {}
28998	    vec_per_axis: Dict[int, List[int]] = {}
28999	    for ax in range(n):
29000	        tile_per_axis[ax] = list(
29001	            loopnest.tile_candidates.get(ax) or defaults["tile"])
29002	        vec_per_axis[ax] = list(
29003	            loopnest.vec_candidates.get(ax) or defaults["vec"])
29004	    smem_cap = None
29005	    if arch in ARCH_TABLE:
29006	        smem_cap = ARCH_TABLE[arch].max_smem_per_block
29007	
29008	    seen: set = set()
29009	    yielded = 0
29010	
29011	    # Reorder permutations, filtered by dep legality. For n=1 this is
29012	    # just (0,); for n=2 it's (0,1) and (1,0) when both legal.
29013	    perms = [p for p in itertools.permutations(range(n))
29014	             if _permutation_respects_deps(p, loopnest.dep_vectors)]
29015	    if not perms:
29016	        perms = [tuple(range(n))]
29017	
29018	    # Parallel subsets, smallest-first.
29019	    par_axes = sorted(loopnest.parallel_axes)
29020	    par_subsets: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = [()]
29021	    for r in range(1, len(par_axes) + 1):
29022	        for combo in itertools.combinations(par_axes, r):
29023	            par_subsets.append(combo)
29024	
29025	    # Tile cartesian product across axes.
29026	    tile_choices = list(itertools.product(*(tile_per_axis[ax] for ax in range(n))))
29027	    # Vec cartesian product across axes.
29028	    vec_choices = list(itertools.product(*(vec_per_axis[ax] for ax in range(n))))
29029	
29030	    # Outer loop ordering chosen so that even small caps surface a
29031	    # diverse spread (one tile × one perm × many par/vec combos
29032	    # before the next tile).
29033	    for tile_tuple in tile_choices:
29034	        tile_map = {ax: tile_tuple[ax] for ax in range(n)}
29035	        if smem_cap is not None and \
29036	                _smem_footprint_bytes(tile_map, n) > smem_cap:
29037	            continue
29038	        for perm in perms:
29039	            for par in par_subsets:
29040	                for vec_tuple in vec_choices:
29041	                    sched = Schedule(
29042	                        tile_sizes=tuple(
29043	                            (ax, tile_map[ax]) for ax in range(n)),
29044	                        fusion_partitions=(tuple(range(n)),),
29045	                        reorder_permutation=perm,
29046	                        vectorize_axes=tuple(
29047	                            (ax, vec_tuple[ax]) for ax in range(n)
29048	                            if vec_tuple[ax] > 1),
29049	                        parallelize_axes=tuple(par),
29050	                    )
29051	                    key = sched.cache_key()
29052	                    if key in seen:
29053	                        continue
29054	                    seen.add(key)
29055	                    yield sched
29056	                    yielded += 1
29057	                    if yielded >= max_schedules:
29058	                        return

29097	        return None

29100	        cursor = loopnest.body_ast
29101	        # Find the innermost for-statement body (or just the function
29102	        # body if no inner for) — that's where the actual compute
29103	        # lives. Walk the cursor preorder collecting every FOR_STMT and
29104	        # take the deepest one's body.
29105	        CursorKind = cindex.CursorKind

29107	        try:
29108	            for c in cursor.walk_preorder():
29109	                if c.kind == CursorKind.FOR_STMT:
29110	                    fors.append(c)
29111	        except Exception as _swexc:
29112	            _debug_swallow('_apply_schedule_lift_body', _swexc)

29116	            # Deepest for-stmt = the one with the most for-ancestors;

29118	            # use the last entry in pre-order traversal as a proxy
29119	            # (deepest cursor of the same kind always appears latest).
29120	            inner_for = fors[-1]
29121	            try:
29122	                children = list(inner_for.get_children())
29123	            except Exception as _swexc:
29124	                _debug_swallow('_apply_schedule_lift_body', _swexc)

29127	            # may collapse the init). The body is the last
